# Naver.com Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/naver-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/naver-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects search results, news articles, and blog content from Naver.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape Naver.com: 2026 Python Guide](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-naver)
- **Code:** [`naver.py`](naver.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Blog post](results/blog_post.json) · [Image search](results/image_search.json) · [News article](results/news_article.json) · [Web search](results/web_search.json)

## What it scrapes

- Naver web search results
- Naver image search reesults

## Functions

- `scrape_web_search(query, max_pages=3, sort=None, period=None, scrape_all_pages=False)` → `{}`: Scrape Naver web search with pagination.
- `scrape_image_search(query, max_pages=3, sort=None, period=None, scrape_all_pages=False)` → `dict[str, Any]`: Scrape Naver image search with pagination. Note: Naver image search doesn't have pagination info it uses scroll to load more results but we can still scraping by using start parameter in re.
- `scrape_blog_post(urls)` → `List[BlogPost]`: Scrape Naver blog posts concurrently.
- `scrape_news_article(urls)` → `List[NewsArticle]`: Scrape Naver news articles concurrently.

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import naver


async def main():
    web_search = await naver.scrape_web_search(query="파이썬", max_pages=3)
    image_search = await naver.scrape_image_search(query="파이썬", max_pages=3, period="6m")
    blog_post = await naver.scrape_blog_post(
        [
            "https://blog.naver.com/cherry_27_/224290687381",
            "https://blog.naver.com/jylove_0120/224289170856",
        ],
    )
    news_article = await naver.scrape_news_article(
        [
            "https://n.news.naver.com/article/001/0015234567",
            "https://n.news.naver.com/article/001/0015234568",
        ],
    )


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields:

- **`SearchWebResult`**: `title`, `url`, `snippet`, `source`, `rank`
- **`SearchImageResult`**: `title`, `link`, `source`, `image_url`, `thumbnail_url`, `img_id`, `color`, `date`, `writer`, `domain`, `rank`
- **`BlogPost`**: `url`, `title`, `content`, `author?`, `date?`, `thumbnail?`, `category?`
- **`NewsArticle`**: `url`, `title`, `description?`, `content`, `press?`, `date?`, `modified_date?`, `images`, `sections`, `origin_url?`

A field marked `?` can be `null`.

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`naver.py`](naver.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `unblocker` = `True`: Scrapfly's [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker), its anti-bot bypass
- `render_js` = `True`: render the page in a real browser
- `country` = `"kr"`: country of the proxy
- `proxy_pool` = `"public_residential_pool"`: proxy pool (datacenter or residential)

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/naver-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_web_search_scraping`, `test_image_search_scraping`, `test_blog_post_scraping`, `test_news_article_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
